title: Closed subsets proper over a base: any scheme structure, closed subsets, images
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to S$ a morphism locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; 'proper over $S$' for closed subsets is as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) For a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ the following are equivalent: $Z$ is proper over $S$; for some closed subscheme structure on $Z$ (a closed subscheme of $X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with underlying set $Z$) the morphism $Z\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]; for every closed subscheme structure on $Z$ the morphism $Z\to S$ is proper. (2) If $Y\subseteq Z\subseteq X$ are closed subsets and $Z$ is proper over $S$, then $Y$ is proper over $S$. (3) Let $g:X\to X'$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$ with $X'\to S$ locally of finite type and separated. If $Z\subseteq X$ is a closed subset proper over $S$, then $g(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X'$ proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), Lemma 0CYN (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base) and Lemma 0CYQ (lemma-functoriality-closed-proper-over-base) part (1)

proof.text: (1), the easy implications. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be closed and let $i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; it is a closed immersion with $i_Z(Z_{\mathrm{red}})=Z$, i.e. one closed subscheme structure on $Z$. By [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1), '$Z$ is proper over $S$' means that $f\circ i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to S$ is proper. Hence: if $Z'\to S$ is proper for every closed subscheme structure $Z'$ on $Z$, it is so for $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$, i.e. $Z$ is proper over $S$; and if $Z$ is proper over $S$, then some closed subscheme structure (namely $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$) is proper over $S$. It remains to show: if $Z'\to S$ is proper for one closed subscheme structure $i':Z'\to X$ on $Z$, then $Z''\to S$ is proper for every other one $i'':Z''\to X$ (Steps 2-4).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), proof, first sentence ('(3) => (1) and (1) => (2) are immediate'); the reduced induced structure is Schemes, Definition 01J4

proof.text: (1), the scheme-theoretic union. Let $i':Z'\to X$ and $i'':Z''\to X$ be closed immersions with $i'(Z')=i''(Z'')=Z$ and $f\circ i'$ proper. Let $i''':Z'''\to X$ be their scheme-theoretic union [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union], the closed subscheme cut out by the intersection of the two ideal sheaves. By that lemma $i'''(Z''')=Z\cup Z=Z$, so $Z'''$ is another closed subscheme structure on $Z$, and there are closed immersions $a':Z'\to Z'''$, $a'':Z''\to Z'''$ with $i'''a'=i'$, $i'''a''=i''$. Since $i'$, $i''$, $i'''$ are injective with the same image $Z$, the maps $a'$ and $a''$ are bijective; in particular $a'$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), proof, sentences 4-6 (scheme theoretic union, Morphisms Definition 0C4H and Lemma 0C4J)

proof.text: (1), $Z'''\to S$ is separated and locally of finite type. The closed immersion $i'''$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), hence locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $f$ is locally of finite type, so $f\circ i''':Z'''\to S$ is locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). The closed immersion $a'$ is universally closed [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](d) and surjective (Step 2), and $(f\circ i''')\circ a'=f\circ i'$ is proper, in particular separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; hence $f\circ i'''$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), proof, sentences 8-9 (Morphisms Lemmas 09MQ, 01T5, 01T3)

proof.text: (1), conclusion. $f\circ i'$ is proper, hence universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], $a':Z'\to Z'''$ is surjective with $(f\circ i''')\circ a'=f\circ i'$, and $f\circ i'''$ is separated and locally of finite type (Step 3); so $f\circ i''':Z'''\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] (quasi-compactness is part of that lemma). The closed immersion $a''$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), so $f\circ i''=(f\circ i''')\circ a''$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a). This proves that properness of one closed subscheme structure on $Z$ over $S$ implies it for every one, and with Step 1 the equivalence of the three conditions in (1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYL (lemma-closed-proper-over-base), proof, sentences 6-7 and 10-11 (Morphisms Lemmas 01W5, 01W3, 03GN; Stacks deduces quasi-compactness separately from the homeomorphism $Z'\to Z'''$, here it is contained in 03GN)

proof.text: (2). Let $Y\subseteq Z\subseteq X$ be closed and $Z$ proper over $S$, so $f\circ i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to S$ is proper (Step 1). As $i_Z$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed set $Z\supseteq Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], $T=i_Z^{-1}(Y)$ is a closed subset of $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $i_Z(T)=Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] there is a closed immersion $j:Y'\to Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $j(Y')=T$. Then $i_Z\circ j:Y'\to X$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] with image $Y$, i.e. a closed subscheme structure on $Y$, and $f\circ i_Z\circ j$ is proper, $j$ being proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c) and properness being stable under composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a). By (1) (some closed subscheme structure proper implies proper over $S$, Steps 1-4), $Y$ is proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0CYN (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base); Stacks omits the proof, this step is written out by the agent from Lemma 0CYL and Morphisms Lemmas 01QS, 01W5, 01W3

proof.text: (3). Let $g:X\to X'$ be an $S$-morphism, $f':X'\to S$ locally of finite type and separated, $Z\subseteq X$ closed and proper over $S$. Then $f\circ i_Z=f'\circ(g\circ i_Z):Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to S$ is proper (Step 1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-image-proper] to $h=g\circ i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to X'$ over $S$: the scheme-theoretic image $i_W:W\to X'$ of $h$ has $f'\circ i_W$ proper, and $i_W(W)=h(Z_{\mathrm{red}})=g(i_Z(Z_{\mathrm{red}}))=g(Z)$ is closed in $X'$. So $g(Z)$ is a closed subset of $X'$ and $W$ is a closed subscheme structure on it with $W\to S$ proper; since $f'$ is locally of finite type, (1) applies to $f'$ and shows that $g(Z)$ is proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].

lean.statement: theorem closed_subset_proper_over_base_properties {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X) : (IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Z ↔ ∃ (Z' : Scheme.{u}) (i' : Z' ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i'), Set.range i'.base = (Z : Set X) ∧ IsProper (i' ≫ f)) ∧ (IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Z ↔ ∀ (Z' : Scheme.{u}) (i' : Z' ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i'], Set.range i'.base = (Z : Set X) → IsProper (i' ≫ f)) ∧ (∀ (Y : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X), Y ≤ Z → IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Z → IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Y) ∧ (∀ {X' : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ X') (f' : X' ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [IsSeparated f'], g ≫ f' = f → IsClosedSubsetProperOver f Z → ∃ W : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X', (W : Set X') = g '' (Z : Set X) ∧ IsClosedSubsetProperOver f' W)
